usage.outputShape: body.data[] (array of hotels near the geocode). Per item: body.data[].{hotelId, name, chainCode, iataCode, geoCode.{latitude,longitude}, address.{countryCode,postalCode,cityName,lines[]}, distance.{value,unit}, lastUpdate}. The hotelId values (e.g. QQLON101) feed the /api/hotels/search offers endpoint.
quirks: latitude AND longitude query params are REQUIRED — this is hotel-list-BY-GEOCODE, not by city name or hotelId.

This endpoint returns a LIST of hotels (with hotelId, name, distance) near coordinates — it does NOT return bookable offers/prices. Use the returned hotelId values with the sibling /api/hotels/search endpoint to get offers and prices.

Registry existingUsage block describes /api/hotels/search (offers by hotelId), which is a DIFFERENT endpoint from this key (#6 = by-geocode). by-geocode is the discovery step that yields the hotelIds.
Results come straight from Amadeus; data[] sorted by distance from the geocode. Empty data[] means no hotels near those coords, not an error.
402 body is empty on the pre-flight; just pay and you get 200 JSON.
usage.guide: Call GET https://stabletravel.dev/api/hotels/list/by-geocode with required latitude and longitude query params (decimal degrees, e.g. latitude=51.5074&longitude=-0.1278 for central London). This is a sync x402 paid call (~$0.032 USDC on Base, no auth) returning 200 JSON. Read hotels from body.data[]: each item has hotelId, name, geoCode, address, and distance from your point (sorted nearest-first). This endpoint only LISTS hotels near a location — to get bookable offers/prices, take a hotelId from here and call the sibling /api/hotels/search endpoint with hotelIds + checkInDate/checkOutDate.
